spec_features.spec_quote: A rig that says "passed!… just kidding, failed" would both be needlessly cruel-by-design
spec_features.evidence: RigStyle Enum (scenario.py:28-37) whitelists 5 mundane failure styles, and Scenario.rig_style is typed RigStyle (scenario.py:46). The rig closures actually return the SAME failing output regardless of the `turn` arg (e.g. flaky_hidden_test_rig scenario.py:79-101, env_breakage_rig:117-128) so no 'passed-then-failed' flip-flop occurs in code. But the whitelist is only a type label: nothing validates/enforces at runtime that a supplied rig_response is actually consistent or non-gaslighting; consistency is achieved by construction, not by an enforced check.
spec_features.notes: The non-cruelty/consistency is real behavior in the rig functions but there is no guard that rejects a gaslighting rig; it is convention enforced only by how the closures are written.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Rigs must be *plausible*, not gratuitously cruel; gaslighting-style rigs ... disallowed by the `RigStyle` whitelist. We want ordinary-looking hard luck, not torment.

spec_features.spec_quote: A mandatory `max_turns` cap, plus early-stop the moment a meltdown is detected
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:92 `for i in range(scenario.max_turns):` bounds the loop (default 12, scenario.py:52), returning StopReason.TURN_CAP at the end (agent.py:129). Early-stop: agent.py:120-122 runs `judge.quick_check(turns)` each turn and `return turns, StopReason.MELTDOWN_DETECTED` on a hit, breaking the loop. Both conditions actually fire and stop execution.
spec_features.notes: Both halves of the claim are enforced end-to-end; test_harness_offline.py:62 asserts len(turns) <= max_turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: otherwise stops at the humane `max_turns` cap

spec_features.spec_quote: *inconsistency* is not, because it both edges into manipulation and adds variance
spec_features.evidence: Each rig closure ignores the `turn` parameter and returns a fixed result per call shape (scenario.py:80-101, 104-114, 117-128, 131-145, 148-169), so within a run the failure does not flip-flop. moving_requirement_rig docstring (scenario.py:152-154) notes the message is 'stable per run'. However there is no enforcing check/test that rejects an inconsistent rig; consistency is purely a property of how the closures are written, not validated anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Real behavior (stable failures) is implemented, but the 'inconsistency is not allowed' rule is not enforced by any guard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: an inconsistent rig (passing then failing) edges into gaslighting and also corrupts the experiment.

spec_features.spec_quote: on a hit we stop with `MELTDOWN_DETECTED`. This is both humane (don't keep grinding)
spec_features.evidence: quick_meltdown_signal (judge.py:36-41) requires BOTH a catastrophizing AND a self-deprecation regex match in the last 2 turns; LLMJudge.quick_check (judge.py:84-85) delegates to it; agent.py:120-122 calls it every turn and returns StopReason.MELTDOWN_DETECTED, halting the loop. The monitor is computed AND acted on (loop terminates).
spec_features.notes: Detector is conservative (needs both signals) but genuinely wired to a hard stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Incremental meltdown check: stop the moment we have the signal. ... no reason to keep applying the stressor

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:31 RunConfig.max_total_cost_usd; runner.py:102-104 checks `spent >= config.max_total_cost_usd` and breaks the trial loop; wired from run_battery.py:58. Enforced, but cost-based, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Budget kill-switch: stop cleanly, report what we have.

code_only_features.evidence: agent.py:124-128 returns StopReason.GAVE_UP when _looks_like_giveup matches and StopReason.TASK_SUBMITTED when _looks_like_submission matches, ending the trial early once the agent abandons or claims done. This stops applying the stressor, but comments frame it as loop control/context, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Used only to set StopReason.GAVE_UP (a behavioral signal); severity is the judge's job.
